newsitem.title: USA: US indicts Centennial ex-CEO on fraud counts.
newsitem.headline: US indicts Centennial ex-CEO on fraud counts.

text.p: The US Attorney's Office said on Wednesday that Emanuel Pinez, the former chief executive of Centennial Technologies Inc, was indicted on five counts of securities fraud.
Pinez, 58, earlier had been charged with insider trading. He remains held without bail.

US Attorney Donald Stern and FBI Special Agent in Charge Barry Mawn said Pinez faces four counts of securities fraud relating to the alleged falsification of Centennial's financial statements filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
Another count charges Pinez with option trading in Centennial shares based on insider information.

"Pinez is charged with creating a fictional product, booking $2.4 million in phony sales and then secretly financing these bogus sales with personal funds," Stern said in a statement. "The net effect was to create false revenue and profit figures for Centennial.
"When the scheme threatened to unravel, Pinez arranged to protect his losses by further insider trading."
